the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يصلي. ﴿وَمَلائِكَتُهُ﴾ Conjoined to what came before. ﴿لِيُخْرِجَكُمْ﴾ The lām is the lām of causation, and the imperfect verb is accusative (manṣūb) by the implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; its fāʿil is latent, and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿إِلَى النُّورِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb as well. ﴿وَكانَ﴾ kāna; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of kāna, placed after. ﴿رَحِيماً﴾ khabar. ﴿تَحِيَّتُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ An adverb of time; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَلْقَوْنَهُ﴾ An imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿سَلامٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ أَجْراً﴾ A past verb and its mafʿūl, and its fāʿil is latent, and لهم is attached to the verb before them. ﴿كَرِيماً﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of أجرا; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يا﴾ A vocative particle. ﴿أَيُّهَا﴾ The one addressed (munādā), whose i'rab was given shortly before; the clause is resumptive. ﴿النَّبِيُّ﴾ badal (substitute). ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna, and nā is its ism. ﴿أَرْسَلْناكَ﴾ A past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿شاهِداً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative. ﴿وَمُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً وَداعِياً﴾ These words are conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to داعيا. ﴿بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to داعيا. ﴿وَسِراجاً﴾ Conjoined to what came before. ﴿مُنِيراً﴾ An adjective of سراجا.

daas-irab:47-48.t: ﴿وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ An imperative verb and its mafʿūl (object), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِأَنَّ﴾ The bāʾ is a preposition and anna is a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl); anna and what follows it are in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) بشر. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of anna. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَضْلًا﴾ The ism of anna, placed after. ﴿كَبِيراً﴾ An adjective (ṣifa) of فضلا. ﴿وَلا﴾ lā is prohibitive. ﴿تُطِعِ﴾ An imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lā, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿الْكافِرِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿وَالْمُنافِقِينَ﴾ Conjoined to what came before. ﴿وَدَعْ أَذاهُمْ﴾ An imperative verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent; the two clauses are conjoined. ﴿وَتَوَكَّلْ﴾ An imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to توكل. ﴿وَكَفى﴾ A past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif because of impossibility (taʿadhdhur). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ The bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and the Divine Name is the fāʿil. ﴿وَكِيلًا﴾ tamyīz (specification); the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:49-50.t: ﴿يا﴾ A vocative particle. ﴿أَيُّهَا﴾ The one addressed (munādā), whose i'rab was given shortly before. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِذا﴾ An adverb of time containing the sense of condition. ﴿نَكَحْتُمُ الْمُؤْمِناتِ﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil, and المؤمنات is its mafʿūl (object); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ A conjunction. ﴿طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾ A past verb; the tāʾ is its fāʿil, the wāw is for lengthening (ishbāʿ), and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) طلقتموهن. ﴿أَنْ﴾ an, making the verb accusative (nāṣiba). ﴿تَمَسُّوهُنَّ﴾ An imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil, the hāʾ its mafʿūl, and the nūn the sign of the feminine plural; an and what follows it are interpretable as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi of the adverb. The meaning of تمسوهن is "have intercourse with them". ﴿فَما﴾ The fāʾ is connective for the apodosis and mā is negating. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) placed first. ﴿عَلَيْهِنَّ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida). ﴿عِدَّةٍ﴾ A noun genitive (majrūr) in form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position, the mubtadaʾ (subject) placed after. ﴿تَعْتَدُّونَها﴾ An imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of عدة. ﴿فَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ﴾ The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil, the hāʾ its mafʿūl, and the nūn the sign of the feminine plural. ﴿وَسَرِّحُوهُنَّ﴾ Conjoined to متعوهن. ﴿سَراحاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿جَمِيلًا﴾ An adjective. ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ Its i'rab was given shortly before. ﴿النَّبِيُّ﴾ badal. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its ism; the nūn of inna was dropped for lightening. ﴿أَحْلَلْنا﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿لَكَ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أحللنا. ﴿أَزْواجَكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿اللَّاتِي﴾ A relative noun in the position of accusative, an adjective of أزواجك. ﴿آتَيْتَ﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَما﴾ The wāw is a conjunction and mā is a relative noun. ﴿مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُكَ﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, and the clause ما ملكت is conjoined. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ min is a preposition and mā is relative (mawṣūliyya); both are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿أَفاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ A past verb, and the Divine Name is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أفاء. ﴿وَبَناتِ﴾ Conjoined to أزواجك. ﴿عَمِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَبَناتِ عَمَّاتِكَ﴾ Conjoined to what came before. ﴿وَبَناتِ خالِكَ وَبَناتِ خالاتِكَ﴾ Conjoined to what came before. ﴿اللَّاتِي﴾ A relative noun, adjective. ﴿هاجَرْنَ﴾ A past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural (nūn al-niswa), and the nūn is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مَعَكَ﴾ An adverb attached to هاجرن. ﴿وَامْرَأَةً﴾ Conjoined to أزواجك, and it is the mafʿūl of أحللنا. ﴿مُؤْمِنَةً﴾ An adjective of امرأة. ﴿إِنْ﴾ A jussive conditional particle. ﴿وَهَبَتْ﴾ A past verb; the tāʾ is for the feminine and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿نَفْسَها﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِلنَّبِيِّ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to وهبت; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is implied (muqaddar). ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿أَرادَ النَّبِيُّ﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿إِنْ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the word of the verse is أَنْ, which the analysis describes.] Making the verb accusative (nāṣiba). ﴿يَسْتَنْكِحَها﴾ An imperfect verb, accusative, and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl of أراد. ﴿خالِصَةً﴾ ḥāl, accusative. ﴿لَكَ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خالصة. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَدْ﴾ A particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿عَلِمْنا﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ A relative noun in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of علمنا. ﴿فَرَضْنا﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them. ﴿فِي أَزْواجِهِمْ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to فرضنا. ﴿وَما﴾ Conjoined to أزواجهم. ﴿مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُهُمْ﴾ A past verb and its fāʿil; the tāʾ is for the feminine and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿لِكَيْلا﴾ The lām is a preposition, kay makes the verb accusative, and lā is negating; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أحللنا. ﴿يَكُونَ﴾ A defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb. ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ A preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of يكون. ﴿حَرَجٌ﴾ The ism of يكون. ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً﴾ kāna, its ism and its two khabars; the clause is conjoined.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ﴾ — (al-Farrāʾ said): Someone may ask: in what respect was the Prophet ﷺ commanded to have taqwā (fear of Allah)?
The occasion for it was that Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb, ʿIkrima ibn Abī Jahl and Abū al-Aʿwar al-Sulamī came to Medina and stayed with ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl and his like among the hypocrites. They asked the Messenger of Allah for things he disliked, and the Muslims were about to attack them. So there came down ﴿يَٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ﴾ with regard to breaking the covenant, because there was a truce between them; so he was commanded not to break the covenant; ﴿وَلاَ تُطِعِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ of the people of Mecca ﴿وَٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ﴾ of the people of Medina in what they asked of you.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ فِي جَوْفِهِ﴾: this was mentioned only because of a man called Jamīl ibn Aws, whose kunya was Abū Maʿmar. He had a good memory and memorised much ḥadīth, so the people of Mecca used to say: "He has two hearts and two minds," because of his memory. He fled in defeat on the day of Badr and passed by Abū Sufyān, who was with the caravan. He said: "How are the people, O Abū Maʿmar?" He said: "Some killed and some fleeing." He said: "Then what is the matter that one of your sandals is on your foot and the other in your hand?" He said: "I thought they were both on my feet." So their lie in saying "he has two hearts" became known. Then He joined to it ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَ﴾.
And His saying: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَ أَزْوَاجَكُمُ ٱللاَّئِي تُظَاهِرُونَ مِنْهُنَّ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ﴾, i.e. this is false, just as your saying about Jamīl is false. If a man says his wife is to him like his mother's back, she is not so; and there is for it the expiation that Allah has appointed. His saying ﴿تُظَاهِرُونَ﴾ without doubling [of the ẓāʾ] was read by Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb. Al-Ḥasan read it (تُظَهِّرُونَ), doubled without an alif. The people of Medina read it (تَظَّهَّرون) with fatḥa on the tāʾ. All are correct and their meanings are close. The Arabs say عَقّبت and عاقبت, ﴿وَعَقَّدتُمُ الأيمَانَ﴾ and ﴿عَاقَدْتُمْ﴾, ﴿ولا تُصعِّرْ خَدَّكَ﴾ and ﴿لا تُصَاعِرْ﴾, "O Allah, لا تُرَاءِبى and تُرأبِّى" [Translator's note: so in the source]. Some people [Translator's note: the source has قولم, apparently for قوم] have read accordingly, saying ﴿يُرَاءُونَ﴾ and ﴿يُرَءُّون﴾, like يُرَعُّونَ. Some have read ﴿تَظَاهَرُونَ﴾, and it is a good form, though I do not know its chain of transmission.
And His saying: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَ أَدْعِيَآءَكُمْ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ﴾.
In the Jāhiliyya, when one of them admired a man's toughness and cleverness, he would take him to himself and give him a share of his inheritance like that of a male child of his. They were attributed in lineage to them, so it would be said "So-and-so son of So-and-so" of the one to whom he had attached himself. So Allah said: ﴿ذَلِكُمْ قَوْلُكُم بِأَفْوَاهِكُمْ﴾, and it is false; ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَقُولُ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾, other than what you have said.

farraa:5-5.t:
Then He commanded them, saying: ﴿ٱدْعُوهُمْ لآبَآئِهِمْ﴾, i.e. attribute them in lineage to their fathers. His saying ﴿فَإِن لَّمْ تَعْلَمُوۤاْ آبَاءَهُمْ﴾: then attribute them in the way you attribute your clients (mawālī) whose fathers you do not know: So-and-so son of ʿAbdullāh, son of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and the like.
His saying: ﴿وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ﴾ in the mistakes you did not intend; the sin is only in what you did deliberately. His saying ﴿وَلَـٰكِن مَّا تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾: (ما) is in the position of a genitive, referred back [as maʿṭūf (conjoined)] to the (ما) that goes with الخطأ [i.e. فيما أخطأتم به].

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلنَّبِيُّ أَوْلَىٰ بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَأَزْوَاجُهُ أُمَّهَاتُهُمْ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbdullāh or Ubayy it is (النَّبيُّ أَوْلَى بالمؤمنينَ من أنفسهم وهو أب لهم) ("and he is a father to them"), and so is every prophet. This came about because the Muslims had been made brothers to one another, and when a man died, the brother with whom he had been paired would inherit from him to the exclusion of his agnates (ʿaṣaba) and relatives. So Allah sent down ﴿النَّبىّ أَوْلَى مِنَ﴾ the Muslims in this standing, and he does not inherit from them — so how should the paired brother inherit from his brother! And He sent down ﴿وَأُوْلُو ٱلأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍ﴾ in inheritance ﴿فِي كِتَابِ ٱللَّهِ﴾, i.e. that is in the Preserved Tablet with Allah.
His saying ﴿مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُهَاجِرِينَ﴾: if you wish, you take (من) as having come in for (أولى): some of them are more entitled to others than the believers and the emigrants are, one to another. And if you wish, you take it — meaning مِن — as intending: those related by blood, from among the believers and the emigrants, are more entitled to inheritance.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحاً وَجُنُوداً لَّمْ تَرَوْهَا﴾: He means: and We sent hosts of angels which you did not see. This was the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq), which is the day of the Confederates (al-Aḥzāb).

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿إِذْ جَآءُوكُمْ مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ﴾: from the side facing Mecca; ﴿وَمِنْ أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾: from the side facing Medina. His saying ﴿وَإِذْ زَاغَتِ ٱلأَبْصَارُ﴾: they swerved away from everything and turned to nothing but their enemy. His saying ﴿وَبَلَغَتِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ ٱلْحَنَاجِرَ﴾: it is mentioned that a man among them would have his lungs swell until they raised his heart to his throat out of terror. His saying ﴿وَتَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلظُّنُونَاْ﴾: the thoughts of the hypocrites.

farraa:11-11.t:
Then Allah said: ﴿هُنَالِكَ ٱبْتُلِيَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَزُلْزِلُواْ زِلْزَالاً شَدِيداً﴾.
He says: they were moved, pushed towards temptation (fitna), but they were protected.

farraa:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿مَّا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ إِلاَّ غُرُوراً﴾: this was the saying of Muʿattib ibn Qushayr al-Anṣārī alone. They have related that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a pickaxe from Salmān to a rock that had defeated them, and struck it three blows, with each of which there was something like a flash of lightning. Salmān said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I saw a wonder in them." He said: the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "In the first blow I saw the white [palace] of al-Madāʾin, in the second the palaces of Yemen, and in the third the lands of Persia and Byzantium (al-Rūm). Allah will surely open to my community as far as they reach." When Muʿattib saw the Confederates he said: "Does Muḥammad promise us that Persia and Byzantium will be opened to us, while one of us cannot go out to relieve himself for fear? Allah and His Messenger have promised us nothing but delusion."

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ مَقَامَ لَكُمْ﴾: the general readership reads it with fatḥa on the mīm, except Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who gave the mīm a ḍamma and said (لاَ مُقَامَ لَكُمْ). Whoever says ﴿لا مَقامَ﴾ seems to mean: no place of standing. Whoever reads ﴿لا مُقامَ﴾ seems to mean: no staying for you; (فَٱرْجِعُواْ).
All the readers we know have the wāw quiescent in (عَوْرَةٌ). It is reported of one of the readers that he read (عَوِرة) on the pattern faʿila, and it is a valid form. The Arabs say: قد أَعور منزلُك ("your dwelling has become exposed") when a weak point (ʿawra) appears in it, and أَعور الفارسُ ("the horseman has become exposed") when there is a gap in his defence open to a blow. Abū Tharwān recited to me:
* لَهُ الشَّدَّةُ الأُولى إذا القِرنُ أَعورَا *
(His is the first charge when the adversary leaves an opening.)
He means the lion. By saying "our houses are exposed (ʿawra)" they only meant: open to thieves, since they were empty of men. So Allah gave them the lie and said: they are not exposed.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ دُخِلَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّنْ أَقْطَارِهَا﴾: meaning the outskirts of Medina; ﴿ثُمَّ سُئِلُواْ ٱلْفِتْنَةَ﴾: He says: a return to unbelief; ﴿لآتَوْهَا﴾: He says: they would have given the fitna. ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it with a long alif. The people of Medina read it short, ﴿لأَتَوْهَا﴾, meaning: they would have done it. Those who lengthen it say: since the asking fell on it, the giving falls on it, just as you say: سألتنى حاجَةً فأعطيتُك وآتيتكها (you asked me for something and I gave it you).
The feminine in His saying ﴿لآتَوْهَا﴾ may also refer to "the deed" (al-faʿla), and the masculine would have been permissible had it come; just as you say about a thing a man does: قد فعلتَها، أما والله لا تذهب بها (you have done it [fem.]; by Allah, you will not get away with it), meaning the deed.
His saying: ﴿وَمَا تَلَبَّثُواْ بِهَآ إِلاَّ يَسِيراً﴾: He says: they would not have remained in Medina after giving in to unbelief except a little, until they perished.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِذاً لاَّ تُمَتَّعُونَ﴾ is nominative [i.e. the verb is indicative], because there is a wāw with it, and when there is a wāw, there is an implied verb in the wāw [i.e. it is joined to what precedes], and the sense of (إذاً) is postponement, i.e. "and if they did that, they would not remain after you except a little, then (idhan)." In one of the two readings it is (وإذاً لا يَلْبَثوا) [Translator's note: the verse discussed here is in fact 17:76, ﴿وَإِذاً لَّا يَلْبَثُونَ خِلَافَكَ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً﴾; this entry is placed at 33:16 in the source], with the nūn dropped, intending the accusative (naṣb). That is permissible, because the verb is left aside, so it becomes as though it begins the speech, even though there is a wāw with it. The Arabs say: إذاً أكسِرَ أنفك (then I will break your nose), إذاً أضربَكَ (then I will strike you), إذاً أغُمَّكَ (then I will grieve you), when they answer a speaker with it. But when they say أَنا إِذاً أضرِبُكَ they put it in the nominative, and treat the verb as having more claim to its noun than إذاً, as though they said: أضربك إذاً. Do you not see that they say أظنُّك قائماً (I think you are standing), giving ẓann (thinking) its effect when they begin with it / 147 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker], but when it falls between the noun and its predicate they cancel it, and when it comes after the noun and its predicate they cancel it. Likewise an oath has an answer (jawāb) when it is put first, so one says: والله إنك لعاقل (by Allah, you are surely intelligent); but when it falls between the noun and its predicate they say: أنت والله عاقل (you, by Allah, are intelligent). Likewise when it is placed last it has no answer, because the speech began with something else. The Arabs may make the verb accusative with إذاً when it is between the noun and its predicate in the case of إنَّ alone, saying: إنى إذاً أضربَك (I would then strike you). The poet said:
لا تَترُكنِّى فيهُم شطيراً * إنى إذاً أهلِكَ أوْ أطيرَا
(Do not leave me among them a stranger; then I would perish or fly off.)
The nominative is permissible. It became permissible with (إنّ) and not with a mubtadaʾ (subject) without (إنّ) only because the verb can never be put first after إنَّ, whereas it could be put first if [إنّ] were dropped.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿أَشِحَّةً عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ is accusative by qaṭʿ (detachment) [Translator's note: al-Farrāʾ's Kufan term for what the Basrans call ḥāl (circumstantial)], i.e. from the nouns that have been mentioned: [those] mentioned of them. If you wish, from His saying ﴿يعوِّقونَ﴾ here at the time of fighting, and they are niggardly about spending on the poor Muslims. If you wish, from those who say to their brothers (هَلُمّ) ("come"), they being thus. If you wish, from His saying ﴿وَلاَ يأْتُونَ البأسَ إلا قلَيلاً أشِحَّةً﴾; He says: cowards in battle, niggardly in spending on the poor Muslims. This is the one I like best. The nominative is permissible as a fresh start (iʾtināf), but I have not heard anyone read it so. (أشحَّة) may also be in [the accusative of] blame, just as one puts the praised into the accusative [of praise]; like His saying ﴿مَلْعُونِينَ﴾.
His saying: ﴿سَلَقُوكُمْ بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدَادٍ﴾: they hurt you with words in time of safety; ﴿بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدَادٍ﴾: sharp.
The Arabs say صَلَقُوكم, but it is not permissible in recitation because it differs from it [i.e. the written text]. One of them recited to me:
أصْلقَ نَابَاه صِيَاح العُصْفورْ * إنْ زَلّ فوه عن جَواد مئشير
(His two canines rang out like a sparrow's cry, if his mouth slipped from a lively, frisky [steed].)
That is when canine strikes canine and you hear its sound.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَ عَنْ أَنبَآئِكُمْ﴾: about the news of the camp in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was.
Al-Ḥasan read it (يَسَّاءلون) (asking one another), and the general readership has (يَسْألونَ), because they only ask others about the news; they do not ask one another.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿لَّقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ﴾: ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd used to read (أُسْوة) with ḍamma on the alif [i.e. the hamza] throughout the Qurʾān, while Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb gave it ḍamma in some places and kasra in others. They are two dialectal forms; the ḍamma is in Qays. Al-Ḥasan and the people of the Ḥijāz read (إسْوَةٌ) with kasra throughout the Qurʾān without varying. The meaning of "uswa (example)" is that they stayed behind him in Medina on the day of the Trench, while wishing in that that the Prophet ﷺ would be victorious, out of anxiety for their town. So He said: there was in the Messenger of Allah a good example, since he fought on the day of Uḥud. That is also His saying ﴿يَحْسَبُون الأحزْابَ لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا﴾, so they are in fear and dread, ﴿وإنْ يَأْتِِ الأَحْزَابُ يَوَدُّوا لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ بَادُونَ فى الأَعراب﴾ (He says: outside Medina). In the reading of ʿAbdullāh: (يحسبونَ الأحزابَ قد ذهبُوا، فإذا وجدوهم لم يذهَبُوا وَدُّوا لو أنهم بادُونَ فى الأعراب) ("they think the Confederates have gone, and when they find they have not gone they wish they were out in the desert among the Bedouin").
His saying ﴿لِّمَن كَانَ يَرْجُو ٱللَّهَ﴾: He restricted it to the believers. Similar in restriction is His saying: ﴿فَمَنْ تَعَجّلَ فِى يَوْمَيْنِ فلاَ إثْمَ عَلَيْهِ وَمَنْ تَأَخَّر فَلاَ إثمَ عَليه﴾ — this is ﴿لمنْ اتّقَى﴾ the killing of game.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَمَّا رَأَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلأَحْزَابَ﴾: they believed and said ﴿هَـٰذَا مَا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾; the Prophet, peace be upon him, had told them that they [the Confederates] would march against him. That is His saying ﴿وَمَا زَادَهُمْ إِلاَّ إِيمَاناً وَتَسْلِيماً﴾. And had it been وما زادوهم ("and they did not increase them"), it would mean the Confederates. [Translator's note: the apodosis "it would be correct" is implied; the source leaves the sentence as given.]
His saying: ﴿وَمَا زَادَهُمْ إِلاَّ إِيمَاناً﴾, i.e. looking / 148 a [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] at the Confederates increased them only in faith.
And He said in another sūra: ﴿لَوْ خَرَجُوا فِيكُمْ مَا زَادُوكُمْ إلاَّ خَبَالاً﴾; had it been مَا زادكم إلا خبَالاً it would have been correct, meaning: their going out would have increased you only in corruption. This is part of the breadth of Arabic that you hear.

farraa:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿مِّنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ رِجَالٌ صَدَقُواْ مَا عَاهَدُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ﴾: "rijāl (men)" is made nominative by (مِنْ). ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَّن قَضَىٰ نَحْبَهُ﴾: his term [of life]. This concerns Ḥamza and his companions.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿وَرَدَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِغَيْظِهِمْ﴾: they had hoped to wipe out the Muslims because of their great numbers, but Allah set upon them a cold wind which prevented any of them from bridling his mount. The horses ran loose in the camp and their tent-ropes snapped, and Allah routed them without fighting, and the angels struck them.
That is His saying: ﴿إذْ جَاءتْكُمْ جُنُودٌ فَأَرْسَلْنَا عليهمْ رِيحاً وجُنُوداً لَمْ تَرَوْهَا﴾, meaning the angels.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنزَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَاهَرُوهُم مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾: these are the Banū Qurayẓa. They were Jews and had helped the people of Mecca against the Prophet, peace be upon him. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is (آزروهم) ("they supported them") in place of ﴿ظاهروهم﴾. ﴿مِن صَيَاصِيهِمْ﴾: from their fortresses. Its singular is ṣīṣiya, which is the tip of a horn and of a mountain. Ṣīṣiya is without hamza.
His saying: ﴿فَرِيقاً تَقْتُلُونَ﴾: meaning killing their men and sparing their offspring.
His saying: ﴿وَتَأْسِرُونَ فَرِيقاً﴾: all the readers agree on kasra on the sīn. تأسُرُون is a dialectal form, but no one read it so.

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَرْضاً لَّمْ تَطَئُوهَا﴾: He meant Khaybar; they had not yet obtained it, and Allah promised it to them.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿مَن يَأْتِ مِنكُنَّ﴾: the readers agree on reading ﴿مَن يَأْتِ﴾ with yāʾ, and they differ over His saying ﴿وَيَعْمَلْ صَالِحاً﴾: ʿĀṣim, al-Ḥasan and the people of Medina read it with tāʾ [i.e. تعمل], and al-Aʿmash and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read it with yāʾ. Those who read with yāʾ made the second verb follow ﴿يَأْتِ﴾, since that is masculine. Those who made it feminine said: since the verb came after هُنَّ ("you women"), it is known to be for a female, so we brought it out according to the meaning. The Arabs say: كم بيع لك جاريةً (how many slave-girls were sold for you — masculine verb), but when they say كم جاريةً بيعت لك they make it feminine, and in both cases the verb belongs to كم; except that when the verb came after الجارية it was taken as feminine. Had it been masculine it would have been correct, because الجارية is explanatory [tamyīz (specification)], and the verb does not belong to it. One of the Arabs recited to me:
أيام أم عمرٍو من يكن عقرَ داره * جواءٌ عدىٍّ ياكل الحشرات
ويسود من لفح السّموم جَبينه * ويَعْرَ وإن كانوا ذوى بكرات
(In the days of Umm ʿAmr, whoever has the hollow of ʿAdī for the heart of his home eats vermin, his brow blackens from the scorching hot wind, and he goes bare, even if they own young camels.) And [also] جواءَ عَدِىٍّ.
Al-Farrāʾ said: I also heard it in the accusative. Had he said (وإن كان) ("even if he is") it would have been correct, and all are good.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَقْنُتْ﴾: with yāʾ; the readers did not differ over it.
His saying: ﴿نُؤْتِهَـآ﴾: the people of the Ḥijāz read it with nūn ("We will give her"). Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read it with yāʾ ("He will give her").

farraa:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ تَخْضَعْنَ بِٱلْقَوْلِ﴾: He says: do not make speech soft; ﴿فَيَطْمَعَ ٱلَّذِي فِي قَلْبِهِ مَرَضٌ﴾, i.e. lewdness; ﴿وَقُلْنَ قَوْلاً مَّعْرُوفاً﴾: sound, not encouraging a lewd man.

farraa:33-33.t:
[His saying]: ﴿وَقَرْنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ﴾: from al-waqār (dignity, staying settled). You say of a man: قد وَقَرَ فى منزله يقِر وُقوراً (he has stayed settled in his home). ʿĀṣim and the people of Medina read (وَقرْنَ) with fatḥa. That cannot be from al-waqār; but we consider that they meant: اقْرَرْن فى بيوتكنّ, then they elided the first rāʾ and its fatḥa was shifted to the qāf; just as they said: هل أحَسْتَ صاحبك (did you perceive your companion? — for أحسست), and as He said ﴿فَظَلْتُمْ﴾, meaning فظلِلْتم.
Some Arabs say واقرِرْن فى بيوتكُنّ, so if someone said وقِرنَ with kasra on the qāf, meaning واقرِرن / 148 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] with kasra on the rāʾ, shifting the kasra of the rāʾ (when it falls away) to the qāf, it would be a valid form. We have not found this, in either of the two forms, used in the speech of the Arabs except in فعلت، فعلتم and فعلنَ; as for the imperative, the prohibitive and the imperfect, no. But we have allowed it because the [final] radical in the feminine plural is quiescent in فعلن and يفعلنَ, so that was permissible. A Bedouin of the Banū Numayr said: يَنْحَطْنَ من الجَبَل (they come down from the mountain), meaning ينحطِطن. This strengthens it.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلْجَاهِلِيَّةِ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾: he said: that was in the period in which the prophet Abraham, peace be upon him, was born. A woman at that time would wear a shift of pearls not sewn at the sides. It is also said: she would wear garments worth a fortune that did not cover her body. So they were commanded not to do the like of that.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَٱلْمُسْلِمَاتِ﴾: someone may say: how is it that He mentioned the Muslim men and the Muslim women, when in meaning one of them would suffice?
That is because a woman said: "O Messenger of Allah, good is only for men; they are the ones who are commanded and forbidden," and she mentioned other things such as the pilgrimage and jihād. So Allah mentioned them [the women] for that reason.

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلاَ مُؤْمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْراً أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلْخِيَرَةُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ﴾: it was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jaḥsh al-Asadiyya. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to marry her to Zayd ibn Ḥāritha, and mentioned that to her. She said: "No, by the life of Allah! I am your paternal aunt's daughter and the unmarried woman (ayyim) of the women of Quraysh." So he recited this verse to her, and she accepted and submitted, and Zayd married her. Then the Prophet, peace be upon him, came to Zayd's house for some need and saw Zaynab in a shift and head-covering, and said: "Glory be to the Turner of hearts!" When Zayd came home, Zaynab told him the story, and he came to the Prophet ﷺ to complain of her to him. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, there is pride in Zaynab, and she hurts me with her tongue, so I have no need of her." The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Fear Allah and keep your wife." He refused and divorced her, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, married her after that. Both things happened — Zayd marrying her and the Prophet, peace be upon him, afterwards — because people used to say "Zayd son of Muḥammad," whereas he was only an orphan in his care. So Allah showed them that he was not his father, since He had forbidden a man to marry his father's wife, or a man to marry his son's wife once [the son] had consummated the marriage.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسِكَ﴾ about marrying her ﴿مَا ٱللَّهُ﴾ will make manifest. ﴿وَتَخْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ﴾: He says: you feel shy before people; ﴿وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ﴾ that you should feel shy before Him.
Then He said: ﴿لِكَيْ لاَ يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ فِيۤ أَزْوَاجِ أَدْعِيَآئِهِمْ﴾.

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿مَّا كَانَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِيِّ مِنْ حَرَجٍ فِيمَا فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُ﴾: in this, and in the nine wives, which were not lawful for anyone else. His saying: ﴿سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: He says: this is a practice that has also gone before for others than you. David and Solomon had the wives we have mentioned, and they were favoured with that; so are you.

farraa:39-39.t: Then He said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُبَلِّغُونَ رِسَالاَتِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: We favoured them with that, meaning the prophets. (الذين) is in the position of a genitive if you refer it back to His saying ﴿سُنَّةَ اللهِ فى الذِينَ خَلوْا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾; if you wish, you make it nominative as a fresh start (istiʾnāf). The accusative of السُنَّة is by qaṭʿ (detachment), as in your saying: فعل ذلكَ سنُة (he did that as a practice). There is much like it in the Qurʾān. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh: (ٱلَّذِينَ بَلَّغُوا رِسَالاَتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَخْشَوْنَهُ) ("who conveyed the messages of Allah and fear Him"). This is like His saying ﴿إنَّ الذينَ كَفَرُوا وَيَصُدُّونَ﴾: yafʿalu is joined to faʿala, and faʿala to yafʿalu. All are correct.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿مَّا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَآ أَحَدٍ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ﴾ is evidence concerning the matter of marrying Zaynab. ﴿وَلَـٰكِن رَّسُولَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: its meaning is: but he was the Messenger of Allah. Had you made it nominative on [the reading] "but he is the Messenger of Allah", it would have been correct, and it has been read so. The preferred form is the accusative.
His saying: ﴿وَخَاتَمَ ٱلنَّبِيِّينَ﴾: al-Aʿmash and the people of the Ḥijāz gave it kasra, and ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan gave it — meaning the tāʾ — fatḥa. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is (ولكن نبيّاً خَتَم النبيِّين) ("but a prophet who sealed the prophets"); this is an argument for whoever says ﴿خاتِم﴾ with kasra. Whoever says ﴿خاتَمَ﴾ means: he is the last of the prophets, as ʿAlqama read, according to what is reported of him, (خاتَمُهُ مِسْكٌ), i.e. its end is musk. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ Sallām ibn Sulaym narrated to us from al-Ashʿath ibn Abī al-Shaʿthāʾ al-Muḥāribī, who said: ʿAlqama used to read (خاتَمُهُ مِسْكٌ) and say: Have you not heard a woman say to the perfumer: "Make its khātam musk for me," i.e. its end?

farraa:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: He forgives you, and His angels ask forgiveness for you.

farraa:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿وَبَنَاتِ خَالِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَالاَتِكَ ٱللاَّتِي هَاجَرْنَ مَعَكَ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is (وَبَنَاتِ خَالِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَالاَتِكَ وٱللاَّتِي هَاجَرْنَ مَعَكَ). The emigrant women may then be from among the daughters of the maternal uncle and maternal aunt, even though there is a wāw, so that He said (واللاتِى). The Arabs qualify [a noun] with a wāw and without a wāw, as the poet said:
فإنَّ رُشيداً وابنَ مَرْوان لم يكن * ليفعل حتّى يُصدر الأمرَ مُصْدَرَا
(Rushayd, the son of Marwān, would not act until he had brought the matter to its proper issue.)
And you say in ordinary speech: إن زرتنى زرتُ أخاك وابن عمّكَ القريب لك (if you visit me, I will visit your brother and your cousin who is close to you), and if you say والقريب لكَ ("and the one close to you") it is correct.
His saying ﴿وَٱمْرَأَةً مُّؤْمِنَةً﴾: you make it accusative through ﴿أحْلَلْنا﴾. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh: ﴿وَٱمْرَأَةً مُّؤْمِنَةً وَهَبَتْ﴾, without (أن) in it, and the meaning of both is the same; as you say in ordinary speech: لا بأسَ أن تستَرِقَّ عبداً وُهبَ لكَ (there is no harm in your taking as a slave a slave who was given to you), and عبداً إن وُهب لك (a slave if he was given to you) — the same. Some read ﴿أَنْ وَهَبَتْ﴾ with fatḥa [on the hamza], on the basis of His saying ﴿لا جناح عليه أن ينكحها﴾ in [the matter of] her having given herself: no blame on him in her gift of herself. Whoever gives it kasra makes it a conditional (jazāʾ). It is like His saying ﴿لاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنآنُ قَوْمٍ أنْ صَدُّوكُمْ﴾ and ﴿إنْ صَدُّوكُمْ﴾. ﴿إنْ أَرَادَ النَّبىُّ﴾ has kasra, and there was no disagreement over it.
His saying ﴿خَالِصَةً لَّكَ﴾: He says: this trait is exclusively yours and a dispensation not for the believers; it is not for the believers to marry a woman without a dowry. Had you made (خالصة) لك nominative as a fresh start (istiʾnāf), it would have been correct; as He said ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إلاَّ سَاعَةً مِنْ نَهَارٍ بَلاَغٌ﴾, i.e. this is a proclamation. Whatever is of the type سُنّة الله, صبغة الله and the like is accusative because it is connected to what precedes it, in the manner of حقّاً ("truly") and the like. The nominative is permissible, because it is like an answer: do you not see that a man says "ʿAbdullāh has stood," and you say حقّا when you connect it [to his words]? When you intend a fresh start, you make it nominative and cut it off from what precedes. This is the pure qaṭʿ (detachment) that you hear of from the grammarians.

farraa:51-51.t:
His saying: ﴿تُرْجِي مَن تَشَآءُ مِنْهُنَّ﴾: with hamza and without hamza, and both are correct. ﴿وَتُؤْوِيۤ إِلَيْكَ مَن تَشَآءُ﴾: this too is among the things with which the Prophet ﷺ was singled out: that he might assign to whichever of them he liked a day, or more, or less, and leave aside whichever of them he wished and not go to her. Before that, each woman of his wives had a day and a night.
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ أَدْنَىٰ أَن تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ﴾: He says: if you did not assign a day to any one of them and they were in that / 149 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] equal, it would be more likely to please them and they would not grieve. It is also said: when they knew that Allah had permitted that to you, they were content, since it was from Allah. It is also said: it is more likely to cool their eyes [with contentment] if other women besides them are not lawful to you. All are good.
His saying: ﴿وَيَرْضَيْنَ بِمَآ آتَيْتَهُنَّ كُلُّهُنَّ﴾: nominative and nothing else, because the meaning is: and each one of them is content. It is not permissible to make ﴿كلّهن﴾ a naʿt (adjective) [i.e. tawkīd (emphasis)] of the hāʾ [pronoun] in the giving, because it would have no meaning; do you not see that you say لأكرمنّ القوم ما أكَرمونى أجمعينَ (I will honour the people as long as they honour me, all of them), and your saying ﴿أجمعونَ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, though the example has أجمعين] has no meaning [with the object pronoun]. Had it had a meaning, its accusative would be permissible.

farraa:52-53.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ أَن تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ مِنْ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾: (أَنْ) is in the position of a nominative; as you say: women are not lawful to you, nor exchanging them. The readers agree on ﴿لاَّ يَحِلُّ﴾ with yāʾ. That is because the meaning is: nothing of women is lawful to you; for that reason the masculine verb was preferred. Had the meaning been for all the women, the feminine would have been better in Arabic. The tāʾ is permissible, since النساء appears overtly without مِنْ.
His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَدْخُلُواْ بُيُوتَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ إِلاَّ أَن يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلَىٰ طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ نَاظِرِينَ إِنَاهُ﴾: غير is accusative because it qualifies the people [addressed], who are definite, while (غير) is indefinite, so it was made accusative "on the verb" [i.e. as ḥāl (circumstantial)]; like His saying ﴿أُحِلَّتْ لَكُمْ بَهِيمَةُ الأَنْعَامِ إلاَّ مَا يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ غَيْرَ مُحِلِّى الصَّيْدِ﴾. Had you put ﴿غَيْرَ نَاظِرِينَ﴾ in the genitive it would have been correct, because before it there is ﴿طعامٍ﴾, which is indefinite, so you would make their action follow الطعام, since the mention of the food returns in (إنَاهُ). As the Arabs say: رأيت زيداً مع امرأة محسنٍ إليها (I saw Zayd with a woman being kind to her — genitive) and محسناً إليها (accusative). Whoever says ﴿محسناً﴾ makes it a description of Zayd; whoever puts it in the genitive, it is as though he said: I saw Zayd with the woman to whom he is kind. When the ṣila (relative clause) belongs to the indefinite noun, you make it follow it, even though it is the action of something else. Al-Aʿshā said:
فقلت له هذه هَاتِهَا * فجاء بأدماءَ مقتَادِهَا
(I said to him: this one — bring her; so he brought a tawny she-camel, he leading her.)
He made المقتاد follow the case of الأدماء, because it is equivalent to your saying "a tawny one whom he leads"; so you put it in the genitive because it is a ṣila for it. It is also recited بأدماءِ مقتادِهَا, putting الأدماء in the genitive by annexing it to المقتاد; its meaning is: with the handful of him who led her. Similar to it in Arabic is your saying: إذا دعوتَ زيداً فقد استغثت بزيدِ مستغِيثِه (when you call on Zayd, you have sought help from the Zayd of the one who seeks his help); the sense of "Zayd" is praise, i.e. he suffices the one who seeks his help. It is not permissible to put it in the genitive on the model of your saying مررت على رجل حَسَنِ وجهه (I passed by a man handsome of his face), because this is not sound until you drop the pronoun referring back to the first, and say: حسن الوجه. It is wrong to say مررت على امرأة حسنِة وجهِها, while حسنِة الوجه is correct.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ مُسْتَأْنِسِينَ﴾ is in the position of a genitive, made to follow الناظرين [as governed by غير]; as you say: كنت غير قائم ولا قاعدٍ (I was not standing nor sitting); and as you say to a guardian: "Eat of the orphan's property in a fair manner, غيرَ متأثّل مالا، ولا واقٍ مالكَ بماله (not amassing wealth, nor protecting your own property with his)." You might make المستأنسين in the position of an accusative, imagining that you make it follow غير, since you have separated the two with words. Likewise, any meaning that admits two forms, when you separate them with words, the second may take a case different from the first. Of that kind is your saying: ما أنت بمحسن إلى مَن أحسن إليك لا مُجْمِلاً (you are not doing good to one who did good to you, nor being gracious), putting المُجْمِل in the accusative or genitive: the genitive by making it follow المحسن, and the accusative by imagining that you had said ما أنت مُحسناً. One of the Arabs recited to me:
ولستُ بذى نَيْربٍ فى الصديق * ومنَّاعَ خَيرٍ وسبّابهَا
ولا من إذا كان فى جانب * أضاع العشيرة واغتابها
(I am not one who sows discord among friends, nor withholder of good and reviler of it; nor one who, when he is apart, neglects the clan and backbites it.)
And Abū al-Qamāqim recited to me:
أجِدُّكَ لستَ الدهرَ رائىَ رامةٍ * ولا عاقلٍِ إلاّ وأنت جَنيب
ولا مصعدٍ فى المُصْعدين لمَنْعِجٍ * ولا هابطاً ما عشت هَضْب شَطِيب
(Truly, will you never again see Rāma, nor ʿĀqil, except as one led along; nor go up with those going up to Manʿij, nor, as long as you live, come down the hills of Shaṭīb?)
And this verse is recited:
مُعَاوِىَ إننا بَشَرٌ فَأَسجحْ * فلسنا بالجبالِ ولا الحديدَا
(Muʿāwiya, we are human, so be gentle; we are not mountains nor iron.)
(الحديدا) is recited both genitive and accusative; most of what I have heard is the genitive. The accusative of المستأنسين may also be through an implied verb, as though He said: then enter not lingering for conversation. There may also be with the wāw an implied [verb of] entering; as you say: قم ومطيعاً لأبيك (stand up, and [do so] obeying your father).
The meaning in the exegesis of the verse is that the Muslims used to come in to the Prophet, peace be upon him, at the time of the midday meal, and when they had eaten they would sit for a long time and ask his wives for things they needed. That became hard for the Prophet ﷺ, until Allah sent down this verse. Some people spoke about it and said: "Are we forbidden to go in to the daughters of our paternal uncle except with permission, or from behind a screen? If Muḥammad dies I will certainly marry one of them." Then the fathers — Abū Bakr and his kin — stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we too not go in to them except with permission, and not ask them for things except from behind a screen?" So Allah sent down ﴿لاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِنَّ فى آبائِهنّ﴾ to the end of the verse. And concerning marriage He sent down ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَؤْذُوا رَسُولَ اللهِ وَلاَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوا أَزْوَاجَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ أبَداً﴾.

farraa:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ بِغَيْرِ مَا ٱكْتَسَبُواْ﴾: it was revealed concerning the people of immorality and lewdness. They used to follow the slave-girls in Medina and commit lewdness with them. The Muslims were living in tents; they had not built or settled. A woman of the Muslims' women would go out to relieve herself, and one of the lewd men would accost her, thinking she was a slave-girl; she would shout at him and he would go away. The dress was the same, so the Prophet, peace be upon him, was commanded: ﴿قُلْ لأَزْوَاجِكَ وَبَنَانِكَ ونساء المؤمنين يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ جَلاَبِيبهِنَّ ذَلِكَ أَدْنَى أَنْ يُعْرَفْنَ فَلاَ يُؤْذَيْنَ [Translator's note: the source has بنانك for بناتك]. The jilbāb is the outer wrap (ridāʾ).
Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn al-Muhallab Abū Kudayna narrated to me from Ibn ʿAwn from Ibn Sīrīn concerning His saying: {يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ جَلاَبِيبهنّ﴾.

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِن جَلاَبِيبِهِنَّ﴾ — thus: he said: she covers one of her eyes and her forehead and the other side, except the eye. [Translator's note: this continues the report from Ibn Sīrīn begun at the end of the previous entry.]

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿لَنُغْرِيَنَّكَ بِهِمْ﴾: the rumour-mongers (al-murjifūn) were from among the Muslims. Those whose hearts were being reconciled (al-muʾallafa qulūbuhum) spread rumours about the People of the Ṣuffa; they would slander the People of the Ṣuffa, alleging that it was they who were approaching the women, because they were unmarried. His saying ﴿لَنُغْرِيَنَّكَ بِهِمْ﴾, i.e. We will certainly give you power over them and set you upon them.
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us / 150 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker]: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: they will not remain your neighbours in it except a short while, until they perish. It is also possible to make "few" a description of them, a description of the cursed, as though you said: except [as] few, cursed; because His saying ﴿أَيْنَما ثُقِفُوا أُخِذُوا﴾ indicates that they will become few and scattered.

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿مَّلْعُونِينَ﴾ is accusative as an [accusative of] reviling (shatm), and also "on the verb," i.e. they will not remain your neighbours in it except as cursed. The reviling is by way of a fresh start, as He said ﴿وَامْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالةَ الْحَطَبِ﴾, for whoever reads it in the accusative. Then He said ﴿أَيْنَمَا ثُقِفُوۤاْ أُخِذُواْ﴾, beginning afresh; this is a conditional (jazāʾ).

farraa:66-66.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تُقَلَّبُ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾: the readers have ﴿تُقَلَّبُ﴾; had it been read ﴿تَقَلَّبُ﴾ ("turn about") and ﴿نُقلَّبُ﴾ ("We turn about"), they would be two valid forms.
His saying: ﴿وَأَطَعْنَا ٱلرَّسُولاَ﴾: one pauses on it with the alif. Likewise ﴿فأَضَلُّونَا السَّبِيلاَ﴾ and ﴿الظُّنُونَا﴾: one pauses on the alif, because it is written in them, and they occur among verses ending in alif. I saw them in the copies of the Qurʾān of ʿAbdullāh without an alif. Ḥamza and al-Aʿmash used to pause on these words without an alif in them, and the people of the Ḥijāz pause with the alif. Their view is dearer to us, because it follows the written text. Had they been read in continuous recitation with the alif it would have been correct, because the Arabs do that. Some have read with the alif both in continuous recitation and in pause.

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّآ أَطَعْنَا سَادَتَنَا﴾: one [word], accusative. Al-Ḥasan read (سَاداتنا), and it is in the position of an accusative.

farraa:68-68.t: His saying: ﴿لَعْناً كَثِيراً﴾: the general readership reads it with thāʾ, except Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, who read it (وَٱلْعَنْهُمْ لَعْناً كَبِيراً) with bāʾ ("a great curse"); and it is so in the reading of ʿAbdullāh. Al-Farrāʾ said: We do not allow it — meaning كثيراً. [Translator's note: so in the source; the reference of "it" is unclear as written.]

farraa:73-73.t: His saying: ﴿لِّيُعَذِّبَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ وَٱلْمُنَافِقَاتِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ وَٱلْمُشْرِكَاتِ وَيَتُوبَ﴾: accusative [subjunctive] by following [what precedes]; if you intend a fresh start (iʾtināf) with it, you make it nominative [indicative], as He said ﴿لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فى الأرْحَامِِ﴾. However, the reading is (وَيَتُوبَ) in the accusative.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿تحيتهم يوم يلقونه سلام﴾: a resumptive statement set out to explain what has been prepared for them in the Hereafter. (تحيتهم): mubtadaʾ (subject), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), being the annexation of the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its object; (يوم): an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (تحيتهم); the clause ﴿يلقونه﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (سلام): khabar (predicate) of (تحيتهم); and the clause ﴿تحيتهم يوم...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿وأعد لهم أجرا كريما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (أعد): past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring to Allah; (لهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أعد﴾; (أجرًا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (كريما): an adjective.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t: ﴿يا أيها النبي إنا أرسلناك شاهدًا ومبشرًا ونذيرًا﴾: (يا): vocative particle; (أيها): (أي) is the one addressed, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and (ها) is for drawing attention; (النبي) is an adjective of ﴿أي﴾. (إنّا): (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters) and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; (أرسلناك): past verb, agent and object; the clause ﴿أرسلناك﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); (شاهدًا): ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf of address in ﴿أرسلناك﴾, and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), i.e. "We sent you destined to be a witness over the messengers and the nations." (مبشرًا): conjoined to (شاهدًا), and (نذيرًا): also conjoined to (شاهدًا).

muyesser-irab:46-46.t: ﴿وداعيًا إلى الله بإذنه وسراجًا منيرًا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (داعيًا): conjoined to (شاهدًا); (إلى الله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (داعيًا); (بإذنه): a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "accompanied by His facilitation." (سراجًا): also conjoined, and (منيرًا): an adjective.

muyesser-irab:47-47.t: ﴿وبشر المؤمنين بأن لهم من الله فضلًا كبيرًا﴾: conjoined to what preceded. (بشر): imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (المؤمنين): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the bāʾ is a preposition; (أن): an abrogating, maṣdar-forming particle; (لهم): the fronted khabar (predicate) of (أن); (من الله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿فضلا﴾; (فضلا): the postponed noun of (أن); (كبيرًا): an adjective of (فضلا); and ﴿أنّ﴾ together with what falls within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the preposition ﴿الباء﴾, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to ﴿بشر﴾.

muyesser-irab:48-48.t:
﴿ولا تطع الكافرين والمنافقين ودع أذاهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (لا): prohibitive; (تطع): imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (الكافرين): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (المنافقين): conjoined to (الكافرين); (دع): imperative verb with a latent agent; (أذاهم): mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), by way of the annexation of the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its agent or to its object, and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلًا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (توكل): imperative verb with a latent agent; (على الله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (توكل); (كفى): past verb; the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) particle, and the Name of Majesty is genitive in form but nominative in position because it is the fāʿil of (كفى); (وكيلا): tamyīz (specification) or ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:49-49.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نكحتم المؤمنات﴾: (يا): vocative particle; (أيها): (أي) is the one addressed, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and (ها) is for drawing attention; (الذين) is an adjective of ﴿أي﴾. (آمنوا): verb and agent, and the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), a clause with no grammatical position. (إذا): an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; (نكحتم المؤمنات): verb, agent and object, and the clause ﴿نكحتم المؤمنات﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it.
﴿ثم طلقتموهن من قبل أن تمسوهن﴾: (ثم): conjunction; (طلقتموهن): past verb; the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent), the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural, the wāw is for lengthening the ḍamma, the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the nūn is a sign of the feminine with no grammatical position; (من قبل): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (طلقتموهن); (أن): maṣdar-forming; (تمسوهن): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن), the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw of the group is the fāʿil, the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi, and the nūn is a sign of the feminine with no grammatical position; and ﴿أنْ﴾ together with the imperfect verb after it is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) in the genitive.
﴿فما لكم عليهن من عدة تعتدونها﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis of (إذا); (ما): negating; (لكم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (عليهن): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿عدة﴾; (مِن): a connective (ṣila) preposition; (عدة): genitive in form, nominative in position because it is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause ﴿تعتدونها﴾ is an adjective of (عدة).
﴿فمتعوهن وسرحوهن سراحا جميلا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition); (متعوهن): imperative verb, agent and direct object; (سرحوهن): conjoined to (متعوهن); (سراحًا): standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); (جميلا): an adjective.

muyesser-irab:50-50.t:
﴿يا أيها النبي إنا أحللنا لك أزواجك اللاتي آتيت أجورهن﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. (يا): vocative particle; (أيها): (أيُّ) is the one addressed, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and (ها) is for drawing attention; (النبي) is an adjective of ﴿أي﴾. (إنّا): (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters) and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause ﴿أحللنا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); (لك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أحللنا); (أزواجك): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (اللاتي): an adjective; the clause ﴿آتيت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿اللاتي﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. (أجورهن): mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وما ملكت يمينك مما أفاء الله عليك﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (ما): conjoined to (أزواجك); the clause ﴿ملكت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. (يمينك): fāʿil (agent) of (ملكت); (مما): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) clarifying ﴿ما ملكت﴾; (أفاء الله): verb and agent; (عليك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أفاء).
﴿وبنات عمك وبنات عماتك وبنات خالك وبنات خالاتك اللاتي هاجرن معك﴾: conjoined to ﴿أزواجك﴾; (اللاتي): an adjective, and the clause ﴿هاجرن﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿اللاتي﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. (معك): an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) (هاجرن).
﴿وامرأة مؤمنة إن وهبت نفسها للنبي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (امرأة): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿أزواجك﴾; (مؤمنة): an adjective; (إن): conditional; (وهبت): past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "she" (هي); (نفسها): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (للنبي): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (وهبت); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, its implied form being "We made her lawful" (أحللناها).
﴿إن أراد النبي أن يستنكحها خالصة لك من دون المؤمنين﴾: (إن): conditional, restricting the first one; (أراد): past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (النبي): fāʿil (agent); (أن): maṣdar-forming; (يستنكحها): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن), and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو), and ﴿ها﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the maṣdar-forming ﴿أنْ﴾ together with the imperfect verb after it is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), the mafʿūl bihi of ﴿أراد﴾; and the second conditional clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (خالصة): ḥāl from the object of ﴿يستنكحها﴾, or from the agent of (وهبتْ), or from ﴿امرأة﴾ because it has been qualified and thereby specified; or it is a naʿt (adjective) of an implied maṣdar, i.e. "an exclusive gift" (هبةً خالصةً). (لك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خالصة); (من دون): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (خالصة) or to a ḥāl from the pronoun in ﴿خالصة﴾; (المؤمنين): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿قد علمنا ما فرضنا عليهم في أزواجهم وما ملكت أيمانهم﴾: (قد): particle of verification; (علمنا): verb and agent; (ما): object of (علمنا), and the clause ﴿فرضنا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. (عليهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فرضنا﴾; (في أزواجهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿فرضنا﴾; (ما): conjoined to (أزواجهم), and the clause ﴿ملكت أيمانهم﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿قد علمنا...﴾ is parenthetical, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿لكيلا يكون عليك حرج﴾: the lām is for causation; (كي): maṣdar-forming and governing the accusative; (لا): negating. (يكون): an incomplete imperfect verb (one of kāna and its sisters), accusative (manṣūb) by ﴿كي﴾; ﴿كي﴾ together with what follows it is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the lām of causation, and the lām of causation and its genitive are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خالصة﴾. (عليك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (يكون); (حرج): the postponed noun of (يكون).
﴿وكان الله غفورا رحيما﴾: (كان) is an incomplete past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; (غفورا): khabar (predicate) of (كان), accusative (manṣūb); (رحيما): a second khabar of ﴿كان﴾.

muyesser-irab:51-51.t:
﴿ترجي من تشاء منهن وتؤوي إليك من تشاء﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. (ترجي): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (مَن): object of (ترجي), and the clause ﴿تشاء﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. (منهن): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿مَن﴾ or from the implied resumptive pronoun, i.e. "whomever you wish to defer from among them." (تؤوي): conjoined to (ترجي); (إليك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تؤوي); (مَن): object of (تؤوي), and the clause ﴿تشاء﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿مَن﴾, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿ومن ابتغيت ممن عزلت فلا جناح عليك﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (مَن): conditional, in the position of the accusative as the fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿ابتغيت﴾, and ﴿ابتغيت﴾ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) in the position of the jussive, and the clause ﴿فلا جناح عليك﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); or ﴿مَن﴾ is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿فلا جناح عليك﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, joined with the fāʾ because the relative is treated like a condition, and the clause ﴿ابتغيت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun ﴿مَن﴾, a clause with no grammatical position, the resumptive pronoun being omitted. The fāʾ is linking; (لا): the lā of generic negation; (جناح): noun of (لا); (عليك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar of ﴿لا﴾; and the clause ﴿ومن ابتغيت...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿ذلك أدنى أن تقر أعينهن ولا يحزن ويرضين بما آتيتهن كلهن﴾: (ذلك): mubtadaʾ (subject); (أدنى): khabar (predicate); (أن): maṣdar-forming; (تقر): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن), and the maṣdar-forming ﴿أن﴾ together with what falls within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "closer to [إلى] their eyes being comforted," the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أدنى﴾. (أعينهن): fāʿil (agent) of (تقرَّ); the wāw is a conjunction; (لا): negating; (يحزنَّ): verb and agent, and the clause ﴿لا يحزنَّ﴾ is conjoined to ﴿تقرَّ أعينهن﴾; (يرضين): conjoined to ﴿تقرَّ أعينهن﴾; (بما): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يرضين﴾. The clause ﴿آتيتهن﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, a clause with no grammatical position. (كلهن): tawkīd (emphasis) of the nūn in (يرضين).
﴿والله يعلم ما في قلوبكم وكان الله عليما حليما﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (الله): mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿يعلم﴾ is the khabar (predicate); (ما): object of (يعلم); (في قلوبكم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, i.e. ﴿يعلم ما استقر في قلوبكم﴾ "He knows what is settled in your hearts," and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. The clause ﴿والله يعلم...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. (كان) is an incomplete past verb (one of kāna and its sisters), and the Name of Majesty is its noun; (عليما): khabar of (كان), accusative (manṣūb); (حليما): a second khabar of ﴿كان﴾.

muyesser-irab:52-52.t:
﴿لا يحل لك النساء من بعد ولا أن تبدل بهن من أزواج﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. (لا): negating; (يحل): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (لك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يحل); (النساء): fāʿil (agent); (من بعد): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (النساء); the adverb ﴿بعدُ﴾ is built (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning. The wāw is a conjunction; (لا): negating; (أن): maṣdar-forming; (تبدل): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن), and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); the maṣdar-forming ﴿أن﴾ together with the imperfect verb after it is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) conjoined to (النساء). (بهن): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تبدل); (مِن): a connective (ṣila) particle; (أزواج): genitive in form, accusative in position as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ولو أعجبك حسنهن﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; (لو): conditional; (أعجبك): past verb, and the kāf is the fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (حسنهن): the postponed fāʿil (agent); the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is implied, indicated by what precedes it; and the conditional clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of (تبدل).
﴿إلا ما ملكت يمينك﴾: (إلا): particle of exception; (ما): a relative noun in the position of the accusative, excepted from (النساء), or in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute); and the clause ﴿ملكت يمينك﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿وكان الله على كل شيء رقيبا﴾: (كان) is an incomplete past verb (one of kāna and its sisters), and the Name of Majesty is its noun; (على كل شيء): a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رقيبًا﴾; (رقيبا): khabar (predicate) of (كان), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:53-53.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوت النبي﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. (يا): vocative particle; (أيها): (أي) is the one addressed, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and (ها) is for drawing attention; (الذين) is an adjective of ﴿أي﴾. (آمنوا): verb and agent, and the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, a clause with no grammatical position. (لا): prohibitive; (تدخلوا): imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), and the wāw of the group is the fāʿil (agent); (بيوت): mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa); (النبي): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿إلا أن يؤذن لكم إلى طعام غير ناظرين إناه﴾: (إلا): particle of restriction; (أن): maṣdar-forming; (يؤذن): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن), passive; (لكم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤذن); (إلى طعام): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤذن), because it has the meaning "unless you are invited to a meal." ﴿أن يؤذن﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "except being given permission." (غير): ḥāl from the agent in (تدخلوا) or from the genitive pronoun in (لكم); (ناظرين): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إناه): mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle (ناظرين).
﴿ولكن إذا دعيتم فادخلوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (لكن): a particle of rectification (istidrāk), lightened and inoperative; (إذا): an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, and the clause ﴿دعيتم﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. The fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (ادخلوا): imperative verb and agent.
﴿فإذا طعمتم فانتشروا ولا مستأنسين لحديث﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (إذا): an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, and the clause ﴿طعمتم﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. The fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (انتشروا): imperative verb, and the wāw of the group is the fāʿil (agent); the wāw is a conjunction; (لا): connective (ṣila), to emphasise the negation; (مستأنسين): conjoined to ﴿غير ناظرين﴾ or to an implied ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "do not enter them barging in, nor lingering," so it is a conjoined accusative; and it has been said that it is genitive, conjoined to (ناظرين). (لحديث): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مستأنسين).
﴿إن ذلكم كان يؤذي النبي فيستحيي منكم والله لا يستحيي من الحق﴾: the clause gives the reason for the prohibition. (إن): an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters); (ذلكم): noun of (إن); (كان): an incomplete verb, and the noun of (كان) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هو); the clause ﴿يؤذي النبي﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (كان), and the clause ﴿كان يؤذي النبي﴾ is the khabar of (إن). (فيستحيي): conjoined to (يؤذي); (منكم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يستحيي﴾; the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; (الله): mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿لا يستحيي من الحق﴾ is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause ﴿والله لا يستحي من الحق﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿وإذا سألتموهن متاعا فاسألوهن من وراء حجاب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (إذا): an adverb for future time containing the sense of a condition, and the clause ﴿سألتموهن﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (اسألوهن): imperative verb, agent and first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (متاعًا): second mafʿūl bihi; (من وراء): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اسألوهن); (حجاب): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿ذلكم أطهر لقلوبكم وقلوبهن﴾: (ذلكم): mubtadaʾ (subject); (أطهر): khabar (predicate); (لقلوبكم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أطهر); (قلوبهن): conjoined to (قلوبكم).
﴿وما كان لكم أن تؤذوا رسول الله ولا أن تنكحوا أزواجه من بعده أبدا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (ما): negating; (كان): an incomplete past verb (one of kāna and its sisters); (لكم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (كان); (أن): maṣdar-forming; (تؤذوا): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن), the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw of the group is the fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the maṣdar-forming ﴿أنْ﴾ and the imperfect verb is the postponed noun of (كان). (رسول الله): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿وما كان لكم...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. (ولا): the wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is for emphasising the negation; ﴿أن تنكحوا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أن تؤذوا﴾; (أزواجه): mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; (من بعده): a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (أبدًا): an adverb, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿إن ذلكم كان عند الله عظيما﴾: (إن) is an abrogating particle, and (ذلكم) is its noun; (كان): an incomplete past verb, and the noun of (كان) is latent (mustatir); (عند الله): ḥāl (circumstantial) from the noun of (كان), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (عظيمًا): khabar (predicate) of (كان); and the clause ﴿كان عند الله عظيما﴾ is the khabar of (إن).

muyesser-irab:54-54.t: ﴿إن تبدوا شيئا أو تخفوه فإن الله كان بكل شيء عليما﴾: (إن): conditional; (تبدوا): the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw of the group is the fāʿil (agent); (شيئًا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أو): conjunction; (تخفوه): verb, agent and direct object, and the clause ﴿تخفوه﴾ is conjoined to ﴿تبدوا شيئا﴾; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), and the Name of Majesty is its noun; (كان): an incomplete verb, and the noun of (كان) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He" (هو); (بكل شيء): a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عليمًا﴾; (عليمًا): khabar (predicate) of (كان); and the clause ﴿كان بكل شيء عليما﴾ is the khabar of (إن).

muyesser-irab:55-55.t:
﴿لا جناح عليهن في آبائهن﴾: (لا): the lā of generic negation; (جناح): noun of (لا); (عليهن): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of (لا); (في آبائهن): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the notion of "being established" (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached.
﴿ولا أبنائهن ولا إخوانهن ولا أبناء إخوانهن ولا أبناء أخواتهن ولا نسائهن ولا ما ملكت أيمانهن﴾: conjoined to what preceded, and the clause ﴿ملكت أيمانهن﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿واتقين الله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (اتقين): imperative verb, conjoined to something omitted, i.e. "comply with what you have been commanded and fear Allah," by way of iltifāt (a shift) from the third person to direct address; the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil (agent), and the Name of Majesty is the object of (اتَّقِين).
﴿إن الله كان على كل شيء شهيدا﴾: (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), and the Name of Majesty is its noun; (كان): an incomplete verb, and the noun of (كان) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He" (هو); (على كل شيء): a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) (شهيدا); (شهيدا): khabar (predicate) of (كان); and the clause ﴿كان على كل شيء شهيدا﴾ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of (إن).

muyesser-irab:56-56.t:
﴿إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), and the Name of Majesty is its noun; (ملائكته): conjoined to the Name of Majesty; the clause ﴿يصلون على النبي﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); (على النبي): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يصلون).
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما﴾: (يا): vocative particle; (أيها): (أي) is the one addressed, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and (ها) is for drawing attention; (الذين) is an adjective of ﴿أي﴾. (آمنوا): verb and agent, and the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, a clause with no grammatical position. (صلوا): imperative verb, and the wāw of the group is the fāʿil (agent); (عليه): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (صلوا); (سلموا): conjoined to (صلوا); (تسليمًا): an emphasising mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:57-57.t:
﴿إن الذين يؤذون الله ورسوله لعنهم الله في الدنيا والآخرة﴾: (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), and (الذين) is its noun; (يؤذون الله): verb, agent and object; (رسوله): conjoined to the Name of Majesty; the clause ﴿يؤذون الله ورسوله﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), a clause with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿لعنهم الله﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); (في الدنيا): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (لعنهم); (الآخرة): conjoined to (الدنيا).
﴿وأعد لهم عذابا مهينا﴾: conjoined to the clause ﴿لعنهم الله﴾. (أعد): past verb, and its agent is latent (mustatir); (لهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعد); (عذابًا): object of (أعد); (مهينا): an adjective.

muyesser-irab:58-58.t:
﴿والذين يؤذون المؤمنين والمؤمنات بغير ما اكتسبوا﴾: (الذين): mubtadaʾ (subject); (يؤذون): verb and agent; (المؤمنين): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (المؤمنات): conjoined to (المؤمنين); the clause ﴿يؤذون المؤمنين والمؤمنات﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), a clause with no grammatical position. (بغير): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤذون); (ما): a relative noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause ﴿اكتسبوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿فقد احتملوا بهتانا وإثما مبينا﴾: the fāʾ is linking; (قد): particle of verification; (احتملوا): verb and agent; (بهتانًا): object of (احتملوا); (إثمًا): conjoined to (بهتانًا); (مبينًا): an adjective; and the clause ﴿فقد احتملوا ...﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (الذين).

muyesser-irab:59-59.t:
﴿يا أيها النبي قل لأزواجك وبناتك ونساء المؤمنين﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. (يا): vocative particle; (أيها): (أي) is the one addressed, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and (ها) is for drawing attention; (النبي) is an adjective of ﴿أي﴾. (قل): imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (لأزواجك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قل﴾; (بناتك): conjoined to ﴿أزواجك﴾; (نساء المؤمنين): also conjoined to ﴿أزواجك﴾, and (المؤمنين): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿يدنين عليهن من جلابيبهن﴾: the clause ﴿يدنين﴾ is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); (عليهن): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يدنين); (من جلابيبهن): a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative as the object of (يدنين), and ﴿مِن﴾ here is partitive.
﴿ذلك أدنى أن يعرفن فلا يؤذين﴾: (ذلك): mubtadaʾ (subject); (أدنى): khabar (predicate); (أن): maṣdar-forming; (يعرفن): an imperfect, an imperfect verb [Translator's note: the word "imperfect" is repeated in the source], indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural, and it is passive; the nūn of the feminine plural is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿أن يعرفن﴾ is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "closer to [إلى] their being recognised." The fāʾ is a conjunction; (لا): negating; (يؤذين): imperfect verb, indeclinable on the sukūn because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural, and it is passive; the nūn of the feminine plural is the nāʾib fāʿil; and the clause ﴿يؤذين﴾ is conjoined to ﴿يعرفن﴾.
﴿وكان الله غفورا رحيما﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (كان) is an incomplete past verb (one of kāna and its sisters), and the Name of Majesty is its noun; (غفورا): khabar of (كان), accusative (manṣūb); (رحيما): a second khabar of ﴿كان﴾; and the clause ﴿وكان الله...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:60-60.t:
﴿لئن لم ينته المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض والمرجفون في المدينة لنغرينك بهم﴾: the lām paves the way for an oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (إن): conditional; (لم): a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and the jussive; (ينته): imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم), and it serves as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (المنافقون): fāʿil (agent); (الذين): conjoined to (المنافقون); (في قلوبهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (مرض): postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the nominal clause ﴿في قلوبهم مرض﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, a clause with no grammatical position. (المرجفون) is also conjoined to (المنافقون); (في المدينة): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (المرجفون). The lām occurs in the response to an implied oath; (نغرينك): imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "We" (نحن), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نغرينك); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
﴿ثم لا يجاورونك فيها إلا قليلا﴾: conjoined to the response to the oath. (ثم): conjunction; (لا): negating; (يجاورونك): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent) and the kāf its object; (فيها): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of (يجاورونك); (إلا): particle of restriction; (قليلا): a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "except a little neighbouring" (إلا جوارا قليلا), or a naʿt of an omitted adverb attached to (يجاورونك), its implied form being "except a short time" (إلا زمنا قليلا); or ﴿قليلا﴾ is a ḥāl from the agent of (يجاورونك), i.e. "except in a state of being few and abased."

muyesser-irab:61-61.t: ﴿ملعونين أينما ثقفوا أخذوا وقتلوا تقتيلا﴾: (ملعونين): ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of (يجاورونك), or accusative by way of censure (al-dhamm); (أينما): a conditional noun governing the jussive, in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أخذوا﴾; (ثقفوا): passive past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw of the group is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (أخذوا): the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), a past verb, also passive, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the jussive, and the wāw of the group is the nāʾib fāʿil; (قتلوا): passive past verb; (تقتيلا): mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and the clause ﴿قتلوا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿أخذوا﴾.

muyesser-irab:62-62.t: ﴿سنة الله في الذين خلوا من قبل ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا﴾: (سنة): mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb from its own root, i.e. "Allah has established that as a practice" (سنَّ الله ذلك سنة). The Name of Majesty: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (في الذين): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (سنة); the clause ﴿خلوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, a clause with no grammatical position. (من قبل): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خلوا﴾; the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; (لن): a particle of negation, the accusative and the future; (تجد): imperfect verb, accusative by (لن); (لسنة): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تبديلا), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi; (تبديلا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:63-63.t:
﴿يسألك الناس عن الساعة﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. (يسألك): imperfect verb, and the kāf is the fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الناس): fāʿil (agent); (عن الساعة): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يسألك).
